pieces.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo), the once-daily GLP-1 pill approved in the US for chronic weight management: what to expect when you start. A fresh 9-minute script written only from the US prescribing information (rev 7/2026) and the Medication Guide, replacing the parked script (5 failures). The parked script is not re-rendered.
pieces.angle:
Keep the brief's structure, with these changes:
- Opening: 'If you're starting orforglipron, the Foundayo pill, the label says nausea is the most likely thing you'll notice. Nausea, vomiting and diarrhea were higher during the dosage escalation period and decreased over time.'
- 15–30 s: −11.1% vs placebo at the highest label dose in Trial 1 (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes).
- Chapter 2: nausea about 35 in 100 vs 10 in 100 on placebo at the highest label dose. Stopping because of adverse events: 10 in 100 at the highest label dose vs 3 in 100 on placebo. Card scope for both: 'pooled Trials 1 and 2: adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes'. Drop 10.3% vs 2.7% entirely.
- Chapter 1: 'once daily, with or without food; swallow tablets whole'. Add 'any time of day' only if found in the PI.
- Chapter 4 pancreatitis: 'Stop taking FOUNDAYO and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting.'
- NAION: the FDA's 9 Nov 2026 Drug Safety Communication on a 'potential' risk, sourced to the FDA page.
- Everything else as briefed.
pieces.working_title: Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill: What Happens When You Start?
pieces.why:
Playbook queue #1 and our strongest signal: drug-name search (the old Foundayo video adds about 60 min a day) plus Foundayo Shorts at 833 and 896 views. The parked script failed 5 times, so this is a fresh script built on the label. | fact-check: The topic is sound and on-pillar. Orforglipron (Foundayo) is FDA-approved and the US PI (rev July 2026) is live at https://uspl.lilly.com/foundayo/foundayo.html. I checked the brief against that PI and found five problems.
(1) The stopping figure in the brief is wrong. 10.3% vs 2.7% is the trial-only 36 mg arm. The label (6.1) says: '8% of patients treated with FOUNDAYO (5.5 mg, 6%; 9 mg, 9%; and 17.2 mg, 10%) … permanently discontinued treatment as a result of adverse reactions compared to 3% of patients receiving placebo.' The 6.1 pool is Trials 1 AND 2, and Trial 2 enrolled adults WITH type 2 diabetes. So the stopping and symptom stats must never be scoped as 'without diabetes' or as 'Trial 1'.
(2) The example opening sentence uses 'mostly', which the brief itself bans. The label says: 'The incidence of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea was higher during the FOUNDAYO dosage escalation period and decreased over time.'
(3) The Medication Guide's pancreatitis action is 'Stop taking FOUNDAYO and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting.' 'Get medical help right away' is NOT the pancreatitis wording, so don't carry it over from the parked fixes for this line.
(4) Section 2, as I found it, says 'once daily, with or without food' and 'swallow tablets whole. Do not break, crush, or chew.' I could not confirm 'at any time of day'. Use it only if the scriptwriter finds that sentence in the PI.
(5) NAION is not in section 5 of the July 2026 PI. Credit it to the FDA Drug Safety Communication of 9 Nov 2026 (orforglipron is named in it), keep the word 'potential', and source it to the FDA DSC page, not a news article.
The −11.1% for the highest label dose in Trial 1 stays as briefed (its population excluded diabetes). Nausea at the highest label dose is 35% vs 10% on placebo, in the pooled Trials 1 and 2. Headache, fatigue and hair loss are confirmed on the common list.

pieces.topic: A quick sting or sore spot during or right after a tirzepatide pen shot: is that normal, what the label counts as an injection-site reaction, and when to call
pieces.angle:
08:00 calm 'Is this normal?' pen moment. Follow the task's length arm and hook archetype.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer): 'Tirzepatide shot stung for a second? The label counts injection-site reactions.' Scene 1's on-screen text matches it.
- Relief fact in the same sentence or the next, no standalone validation line: injection-site reactions were reported in 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo (Zepbound PI rev. 28 Aug 2026, section 6.1). Population on the card: adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition. Say 'pain' is one of the included terms only if section 6.1 lists it. Otherwise say 'reactions at the injection site' with the label's own term list.
- Rotation: credit 'change (rotate) your injection site each week' only to the single-dose pen IFU at its own URL, quoted only if it loads.
- Untagged red flags: spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever means call your prescriber.
- Allergy emergency card with the full list: swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat; trouble breathing or swallowing; severe rash or itching; fainting or feeling dizzy; very rapid heartbeat. Action: stop using it and get medical help right away, or call your local emergency number. Then 'For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.'
- Scope card: US single-dose pen; KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets.
- Leave out: technique beyond the IFU, warm-up steps, doses.
- Close with 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and a loop line back to sentence 1. No subscribe line, no link line. 160 words or fewer.
- Post note (Exp G): target is the Pen how-to video.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Shot Stings for a Second: Normal? #shorts
pieces.why: Visible pen 'Is this normal?' moments are our most proven Short format (279, 213, 181; 1,306 on TikTok). The angle (a sting or sore spot) differs from the bruise, blood-drop and click Shorts.

pieces.topic: Headache since starting orforglipron (Foundayo)? Headache is on the US label's common list
pieces.angle:
Sentence 1: 'Headache since starting Foundayo, orforglipron? It's on the label's common list.'
- Optional stat: 'About 9 in 100 at the highest label dose had headache, versus 7 in 100 on placebo.'
- Card scope: 'Foundayo US label, pooled Trials 1 and 2: adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes'.
- If space is tight, use the label wording only and no number.
- Keep the tips, the pharmacist line, the emergency headache line and the fixed don't-stop line as briefed.
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1. It pairs an approved drug name with a felt symptom, our strongest Short signal (Foundayo nausea 833 views, Foundayo Thanksgiving 896), and sends viewers to the Foundayo long video. | fact-check: Headache is confirmed on the Foundayo PI (rev July 2026) Table 1 common list: 9% at the highest label dose vs 7% on placebo. But Table 1 pools Trials 1 and 2, and Trial 2 enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes. So the briefed population ('Trial 1, adults without diabetes') is wrong for this stat. The difference vs placebo is small (2 percentage points), so don't frame headache as caused by the drug. The brief already says not to name a cause.
